questions.question: What is the correct way to check whether a %Status value indicates an error?

options.text: Both B and C are valid

questions.explanation: Both $$$ISERR(sc) (the macro) and sc '= $$$OK (direct comparison) correctly detect an error status. IF sc = 0 is wrong because $$$OK is 1, not 0.

questions.question: What does the following code print?
What does $FIND("Hello World", "World") return?
questions.explanation: $FIND returns the position after the found substring. 'World' starts at position 7 and is 5 characters long, so $FIND returns 7 + 5 = 12.

questions.question: Which of the following macros are valid for working with %Status values? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: $$$OK, $$$ISERR, $$$ISOK, and $$$ThrowOnError are all standard IRIS macros for %Status handling. $$$STATUSERROR does not exist as a standard macro.

questions.question: You call person.%Save() inside a TRY block. Which line correctly throws an exception if the save fails?
questions.explanation: $$$ThrowOnError(sc) is the idiomatic macro that throws an exception if sc is an error status. It is the shortest and most readable pattern inside a TRY block.

questions.question: What does $HOROLOG return?

options.text: The current date in YYYY-MM-DD format
Two comma-separated integers representing days since Dec 31, 1840 and seconds since midnight
The current time in HH:MM:SS format

questions.explanation: $HOROLOG returns a string in the format days,seconds where days are counted from December 31, 1840 and seconds since midnight.

questions.question: In ObjectScript, what is the result of the expression "10" > "9"?

options.text: Error — mixed types cannot be compared

questions.explanation: In ObjectScript, when both operands look numeric, comparison is numeric. 10 > 9 is 1 (True).

questions.question: Which of the following are valid ways to pass a local array into a method? (select all that apply)

options.text: Declare ByRef pArr in the method signature and call with .arr
Declare pArr As %Array in the signature
Use MERGE to copy the array to a global, then pass the global name as a string
Use ByRef and call with ..Method(.myArr) from an instance method

questions.explanation: Both are correct ways to pass arrays by reference: declaring ByRef pArr and calling with a . prefix. B is wrong (%Array is not a valid parameter type for multidimensional arrays). C is a workaround, not the standard pattern.
